sheet-1-1.description: This part is the whole of sheet 1 of West Long Branch apart from the inset at its right, and shows the centre of the village around the junction of Lippencott's Road, Monmouth Road and Cedar Avenue, drawn at 60 ft to an inch with north toward the upper left. Wall runs diagonally across the upper half of the sheet, from the left edge toward the upper right, and meets Lippencott's Road in a wide open junction near the top centre; Lippencott's Road runs straight down the middle of the sheet to its junction with Monmouth, the road lettered Road leading south, and Cedar Avenue leading east. Monmouth runs from Wall at the left edge to that junction. The buildings are almost all frame dwellings with outbuildings on large lots. Along Lippencott's Road stand the 1st M.E. Church, lit by electricity and heated by furnace, with a Sunday school, horse sheds and the public school behind them to the west. Near the central junction are a dry goods and grocery store, J. Short's carriage shop with blacksmith, painting and wheelwright rooms, a separate blacksmith shop, a fire department house with a combination hook and ladder and chemical engine and a hose cart, a marble works on Wall, and long hen houses on the lots south of Monmouth. A large cemetery fills the area east of Lippencott's Road between Wall and the lots on Cedar Avenue. A 6 inch water pipe is drawn along Cedar Avenue and toward the fire department. The title block gives a population of 600, one independent hose cart and water facilities described in the Long Branch report. The sheet margins are marked vacant beyond and no exposure.
notes: Lippencott's Road is today Locust Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Wall is today Wall Street; Monmouth is today Monmouth Road; Cedar Avenue keeps its name.
The road south of the central junction is lettered only ROAD; it is today Monmouth Road.
Drawn at 60 ft to an inch, an unusual scale; the fit gives about 3 percent fewer pixels per foot than the sister 1907 New Jersey coast atlases, so the sheet may be drawn slightly off scale.
Placed from three street junctions and three parcel block corners next to them; nothing east of the cemetery or along outer Cedar Avenue and Wall is controlled.

Sheet 1, Scale 60 ft to an inch; north toward upper left. Village centre: Wall St, Lippencott's Road (now Locust Avenue), Monmouth Road and Cedar Av around the 1st M.E. Church and cemetery. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset of Frank Dennis Ice Houses on a pond, 3/4 mile NE of the M.E. Church (not placed). Only three modern junctions on the sheet; three parcel block corners added.
